references.text: The Lord reveals himself to Moses and proclaims his nature: 'The Lord, the Lord is a merciful and gracious God' – God alone is the source of all goodness (2 Mos 34:6-7).
'Praise the Lord, for he is good; his mercy endures forever' – God's goodness is supreme and eternal (1 Chr 16:34).
'The Lord is good and righteous' – the psalmist affirms that goodness is a fundamental attribute of God (Ps 25:8).
'For the Lord is good; his mercy endures forever' – God's goodness is absolute and without end, supporting Jesus' words that only God is good (Ps 100:5).
'Praise the Lord! Praise the Lord, for he is good; his mercy endures forever' – a return to God's supreme goodness (Ps 106:1).
'Praise the Lord, for he is good; his mercy endures forever' – God's goodness is unique and unchanging (Ps 118:1).
'The Lord is good to all; his mercy is over all that he has made' – God's goodness is universal and absolute (Ps 145:9).
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus says, 'Why do you ask me about what is good? One there is who is good.' This confirms that only God is absolutely good (Matt 19:17).
Mark's parallel account where Jesus answers, 'Why do you call me good? No one is good except one – God.' The same statement rendered in another gospel tradition (Mk 10:18).
'Every good gift and every perfect gift comes from above, from the Father of lights' – James confirms that all goodness has its origin in God alone (Jas 1:17).
